causal_boundary: If the decoded reset path runs after a snooze is committed, that scheduled row is removed. Candidate06 does not contain enough independent durable snooze state to reconstruct that requested time. This is a concrete source-level recovery gap, not a claim that a device reboot or live reset was executed.
facts: Actual CalendarReceiver accepts BOOT_COMPLETED and its async body calls removeScheduledAlarms, which updates SCHEDULE_ALARM_REMOVE_URI.
Actual CalendarAlarmManager.runScheduleNextAlarm(true, provider) begins one transaction and calls removeScheduledAlarmsLocked before rescheduling.
Actual removeScheduledAlarmsLocked deletes CalendarAlerts where state=0, with no exception for future alarms or minutes=0 snoozes.
The normal non-reset stale-alert cleanup does explicitly retain minutes=0 when there is no matching Reminders row; this exception does not exist in reset.

The actual future alarm search uses Instances joined with Reminders and skips already represented event/begin/alarm tuples; it cannot derive an arbitrary ten-minute user snooze time from an ordinary reminder definition.

Candidate06 stores a snooze as a new state=0 minutes=0 CalendarAlerts row and arms its one-shot before its no-yield batch. It has no independent persisted user snooze intent and no future snooze restoration in boot/refresh handlers.

host_sql_counterexample.qualification: Exact decoded predicate exercised on host SQLite only

known_chain_limit: CalendarProviderJobService body and PostInitializeThread are not in this four-class decode. The final async delivery from the boot remove URI to the reset boolean is not independently completed here; the directly decoded reset method effect itself is exact.
next_fix_direction: Keep ordinary reminder scheduling in CalendarProvider. Persist only an authenticated user snooze request, bind it to the original event/occurrence and state transition, and reconcile its owned wakeup/row after provider reset or reboot without resurrecting dismissed/deleted/changed events. Do not simply mirror all future Reminders or treat a CalendarAlerts row as reboot persistence.
